challenges.title: Hello, World — Your Dev Environment
challenges.description: Set up your local development environment. This is the foundation everything else builds on. A bad environment setup causes 90% of beginner frustration.
challenges.context: Before you write a single line of code that matters, your machine needs to be ready. Today is about getting your tools right so tomorrow you can focus entirely on building.
objectives: Install Node.js 20+ and verify with node --version
Install VS Code with essential extensions
Configure Git with your name and email
Create a GitHub account and SSH key pair
Push your first commit to a new repository

buildSteps.title: Install Node.js
buildSteps.description: Download and install Node.js 20 LTS from nodejs.org. Verify with node --version and npm --version.

buildSteps.title: Set up VS Code
buildSteps.description: Install VS Code and the extensions: ESLint, Prettier, GitLens, and One Dark Pro theme.

buildSteps.title: Configure Git
buildSteps.description: Run git config --global user.name and user.email. This marks your commits with your identity.

buildSteps.title: Create SSH key
buildSteps.description: Generate an SSH key pair and add the public key to your GitHub account settings.

buildSteps.title: First commit
buildSteps.description: Create a new repo, write a README, and push. This proves your entire stack works end-to-end.

deliverables.label: GitHub repository with your setup notes
Terminal showing node, git, npm versions
LinkedIn post: Day 1 of your journey

resources.title: VS Code Setup for Web Dev 2025
SSH Keys for GitHub
resources.description: Step-by-step SSH key generation and GitHub setup

tips.text: Don't skip SSH setup — you'll thank yourself in week 2 when you're pushing code every day.
Install the Prettier extension in VS Code right now. Future you will be grateful.

challenges.title: Build a REST API with Express & MongoDB
challenges.description: Today you build a full REST API from scratch — routes, controllers, middleware, and a real database. This is the backbone of every web application you'll build from here.
challenges.context: You've spent 11 days learning how the web works. Today you put it all together. By end of day, you'll have a working API that a frontend can talk to. This is a major milestone — most students feel a real confidence shift after Day 12.
objectives: Initialize a Node.js project with Express 5
Connect to MongoDB Atlas using Mongoose
Build CRUD routes for a 'todos' resource
Test all endpoints with Thunder Client or Postman
Handle errors globally with an error middleware

buildSteps.title: Initialize the project
buildSteps.description: Run npm init, install express, mongoose, dotenv, and cors. Set up folder structure: routes/, controllers/, models/, middleware/.

buildSteps.title: Connect to MongoDB Atlas
buildSteps.description: Create a free cluster, get your connection string, and connect using Mongoose. Store URI in .env — never commit it.

buildSteps.title: Build CRUD routes
buildSteps.description: Create a Todo model with Mongoose. Build GET all, POST create, PUT update, DELETE remove routes in /routes/todos.js.

buildSteps.title: Add validation middleware
buildSteps.description: Validate request bodies before hitting the database. Reject bad input early — write the validateTodo middleware.

buildSteps.title: Test & document
buildSteps.description: Test every endpoint with Postman or Thunder Client. Write a brief README explaining your routes with example requests.

deliverables.label: GitHub repository with clean, documented code
Specific commit showing today's API work
LinkedIn post about what you built today

tips.text: Don't hardcode your MongoDB URI. Use a .env file and dotenv from Day 1. This habit saves you from accidental credential leaks.
Write your error middleware last, after all routes. Express processes middleware in order — this is a common gotcha.
Test each route as you build it — don't wait until the end. 4 working routes > 8 broken ones.
Build the simplest version first. Get one route working end-to-end before adding the rest. Seeing data flow is motivating.

challenges.title: Authentication with JWT
challenges.description: Protect your API. Today you add signup, login, and route protection using JSON Web Tokens.
challenges.context: An API that anyone can access isn't production-ready. Today you learn the most widely-used auth pattern in Node.js.
objectives: Create user model with hashed passwords (bcrypt)
Build an auth middleware to protect routes
Test with invalid tokens and expired tokens

buildSteps.title: Create the User model
buildSteps.description: Define a Mongoose User schema with email and password fields. Hash the password with bcrypt before saving.

buildSteps.title: Build auth routes
buildSteps.description: Create POST /auth/signup and POST /auth/login. Return a JWT on successful login.

buildSteps.title: Generate JWT tokens
buildSteps.description: Use jsonwebtoken to sign tokens with your secret. Set a reasonable expiry (e.g. 7d).

buildSteps.title: Protect routes
buildSteps.description: Write an authMiddleware that reads the Authorization header and verifies the token.

buildSteps.title: Test edge cases
buildSteps.description: Test with missing tokens, expired tokens, and tampered tokens. All should return 401.

deliverables.label: LinkedIn post explaining JWT to beginners

resources.title: JWT Authentication in Node.js
resources.description: Complete JWT auth implementation from scratch

resources.title: jsonwebtoken npm documentation
resources.description: Official API reference for sign, verify, and decode

tips.text: Store your JWT_SECRET in .env. Never hardcode it. Use a long random string — at least 32 characters.
